nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If the concatenated sentential form $u v$ yields the terminal word $w$, then there are terminal words $w_1$ and $w_2$ with $w = w_1 w_2$ such that $u$ yields $w_1$ and $v$ yields $w_2$.
nodes.title: Splitting a yield over a concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If the sentential form $u$ yields the terminal word $w_1$ and the sentential form $v$ yields the terminal word $w_2$, then the concatenated form $u v$ yields $w_1 w_2$.
nodes.title: Concatenation of yields

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and let $u$, $u'$, $v$, $v'$ be sentential forms of $g$. If $u$ derives $u'$ and $v$ derives $v'$ in $g$ (each in zero or more steps), then the concatenation $uv$ derives $u'v'$ in $g$.
nodes.title: Concatenating derivations

nodes.summary: Let $g$ and $G$ be context-free grammars over the same terminal alphabet, and let $f$ map the nonterminals of $g$ to those of $G$. Extend $f$ to symbols and sentential forms by renaming each nonterminal and keeping each terminal. Suppose that for every production $A \to \alpha$ of $g$, the renamed production $f(A) \to f(\alpha)$ is a production of $G$. Then whenever a sentential form $u$ derives $v$ in $g$ (in zero…
nodes.title: Derivations transfer along a renaming of nonterminals

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and assign to each nonterminal $A$ of $g$ the language of terminal words that $g$ derives from $A$. If a terminal word $w$ lies in the language that a sentential form $u$ of $g$ denotes under this assignment, then $u$ derives $w$ in $g$.
nodes.title: Words of the canonical interpretation are derivable

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If the sentential form $u$ yields the terminal word $w$, then $u$ derives $w$, read as a string of terminal symbols, in $g$: that is, $u \Rightarrow^* w$ in zero or more rewriting steps.
nodes.title: Yields are derivable

nodes.summary: For every assignment $V$ of languages to nonterminals and all sentential forms $u$ and $v$, the language that $uv$ denotes under $V$ is the concatenation of the languages that $u$ and $v$ denote under $V$.
nodes.title: Interpretation of a concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $V$ a valuation of $g$. If a sentential form $u$ derives $v$ in $g$ (in zero or more steps), then the language that $v$ denotes under $V$ is contained in the language that $u$ denotes under $V$.
nodes.title: Derivations shrink interpretations under a valuation

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $V$ a valuation of $g$. If a sentential form $u$ rewrites to $v$ by one production of $g$, then the language that $v$ denotes under $V$ is contained in the language that $u$ denotes under $V$.
nodes.title: A production step shrinks interpretations under a valuation

nodes.summary: Under every assignment of languages to nonterminals, a terminal word $w$, read as a sentential form, denotes the singleton language $\{w\}$.
nodes.title: A terminal word denotes its singleton

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon N \to N'$ be a map of nonterminals, extended to sentential forms by renaming each nonterminal and keeping each terminal, and let $V$ assign a language to each nonterminal in $N'$. For every sentential form $u$ over $N$, the language that $f(u)$ denotes under $V$ equals the language that $u$ denotes under the assignment $V \circ f$.
nodes.title: Interpretation after renaming nonterminals

nodes.summary: Under an assignment $V$ of languages to nonterminals, a sentential form denotes the concatenation, in order, of the languages its symbols denote: a terminal $a$ denotes the language containing only the one-letter word $a$, and a nonterminal $A$ denotes $V(A)$. The empty sentential form denotes the language containing only the empty word.
nodes.title: Interpretation of a sentential form

nodes.summary: Under an assignment $V$ of languages to nonterminals, a terminal $a$ denotes the language containing only the one-letter word $a$, and a nonterminal $A$ denotes its assigned language $V(A)$.
nodes.title: Interpretation of a grammar symbol

nodes.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$, the assignment that sends each nonterminal $A$ of $g$ to the language generated by $g$ from $A$ is a valuation of $g$.
nodes.title: The languages generated from each nonterminal form a valuation

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar with terminals $T$, and let $V$ assign a language over $T$ to each nonterminal of $g$. Interpret a sentential form under $V$ by sending each terminal $a$ to the language $\{a\}$ of the one-letter word $a$ and each nonterminal $B$ to $V(B)$, and concatenating these languages in order (the empty form is interpreted as $\{\varepsilon\}$). Then $V$ is a *valuation* of $g$ when, for…
nodes.title: Valuation of a grammar

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$ and a nonterminal $A$ of $g$, the language generated by $g$ from $A$ is the set of words $w$ over the terminals of $g$ such that $g$ derives $w$ from the one-symbol sentential form $A$. It is the language of $g$ with $A$ in place of the initial nonterminal.
nodes.title: Language generated from a nonterminal

nodes.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$ and every valuation $V$ of $g$, the language generated by $g$ is contained in $V(S)$, where $S$ is the initial nonterminal of $g$.
nodes.title: Valuations bound the language of a grammar

nodes.summary: Let $f$ map nonterminals $N$ to nonterminals $N'$, and let $w$ be a word over the terminals. Reading $w$ as a sentential form over $N$ and renaming its nonterminals by $f$ gives $w$ read as a sentential form over $N'$.
nodes.title: Renaming nonterminals fixes terminal words

nodes.summary: If $f$ is an injective map from nonterminals $N$ to nonterminals $N'$, then renaming the nonterminals of productions over $N$ by $f$ is injective: two productions with the same renaming are equal.
nodes.title: Injective renamings are injective on productions

nodes.summary: Given a map $f$ from nonterminals $N$ to nonterminals $N'$, the renaming by $f$ of a production $A \to u$ is the production $f(A) \to u'$, where $u'$ is obtained from $u$ by replacing each nonterminal $B$ with $f(B)$ and leaving each terminal unchanged.
nodes.title: Renaming the nonterminals of a production

nodes.summary: If $f$ is an injective map from nonterminals $N$ to nonterminals $N'$, then renaming grammar symbols by $f$, which fixes each terminal and sends each nonterminal $A$ to $f(A)$, is injective.
nodes.title: Injective renamings are injective on symbols

nodes.summary: Given a map $f$ from nonterminals $N$ to nonterminals $N'$, renaming a grammar symbol by $f$ leaves a terminal $a$ unchanged and sends a nonterminal $A$ to the nonterminal $f(A)$.
nodes.title: Renaming the nonterminals of a symbol

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar with initial nonterminal $S$. A terminal word $w$ belongs to the language of $g$ if and only if the one-symbol sentential form $S$ yields $w$.
nodes.title: Language membership through yields

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $T$, the language over $T$ whose only word is the empty word is context-free: a grammar with one nonterminal and a single production erasing it generates this language.
nodes.title: The language of the empty word is context-free

nodes.summary: For every word $w$ over an alphabet $T$, the language $\{w\}$ consisting of $w$ alone is context-free: one production spells the word out.
nodes.title: Singleton languages are context-free

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar, $u$ a sentential form of $g$ and $w$ a word of terminals. Then $u$ yields $w$ in $g$ if and only if $u$ derives in $g$, by zero or more rewriting steps, the sentential form consisting of the letters of $w$ read as terminals.
nodes.title: Yields coincide with derivations of terminal words

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If the sentential form $u$ derives the terminal word $w$, read as a string of terminal symbols, in $g$, then $u$ yields $w$.
nodes.title: Derivable terminal words are yields

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $A \to \alpha$ a production of $g$. If $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$, then the one-symbol sentential form $A$ yields $w$.
nodes.title: Yield through one production

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$ with terminal alphabet $T$, the relation "the sentential form $u$ yields the terminal word $w$" is the smallest relation such that: the empty form yields the empty word; if $u$ yields $w$, then for every terminal $a$ the form $a u$ yields $a w$; and if $A \to \alpha$ is a production of $g$, $\alpha$ yields $w_1$ and $u$ yields $w_2$, then the form $A u$ yields $w_1 w_2$.
nodes.title: Yield of a sentential form

nodes.summary: The empty language over any alphabet is context-free: take a grammar with no productions.
nodes.title: The empty language is context-free

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
